Machine-authored live request 34071a88f5e74d9bb6a7e4fa9173f2ff.

For a source a/b with b≥5 write n=b−2, m=a−1, N=b−1. The inherited exact second-row
formula is 2[v²]P=u^m(1+u)^(n−3)Q(u), where
Q=[4t, 9m²+13m+6, 6m²+6mn+8m+6n+6, (m+n+2)(m+n+1)].
The source statistic obeys 0≤t≤2m, m≤n and either n≤2m or t=0.
These are source-derived restrictions; they do not hold for arbitrary weighted
transfer systems.

For 0≤h≤n, at i=m+h set k=h+1=i+2−a. Let F(k)=secondNorm340(k,N,m,t), explicitly the
quartic falling-factorial expression in the Lean module. The new checked coefficient
bridge establishes

    2 N(N−1)(N−2)(N−3) A(i,2) = choose(N,k) F(k).

For 1≤k and k+2≤N, the normalized gap G(t)=F(k+1)^2−F(k)F(k+2) is quadratic in t. Its exact
Bernstein identity is

    (2m)^2 G(t) = (2m−t)^2 G(0) + t(2m−t) B + t² G(2m),

where B=2F_1(0)F_1(2m)−F_0(0)F_2(2m)−F_0(2m)F_2(0).
G(0) has nonnegative polynomial coefficients after k=1, k=2, or k=x+3
and the appropriate nonnegative distance from the last index. For the other
two terms, homogenizing m over n/2≤m≤n introduces the nonnegative variables
2m−n and n−m; multiplying by n^4 yields polynomial certificates with
nonnegative coefficients. Lean checks their identities by ring arithmetic
and signs by order reasoning. This proves the algebraic normalized inequality
under the precise source restriction; it does not prove arbitrary-word closure.

The resulting source strengthening compares the unchanged raw coefficients:

    (k+2)(N−k) A(i,2) A(i+2,2)
       ≤ (k+1)(N−k−1) A(i+1,2)^2.

The source bridge retains zeros, uses the original polygon guard, and cancels

Replace the common x in the positive ambient transfer at each site by a
separate variable. The new siteEval340 specializes exactly to the inherited
transfer when those variables coincide, with a universal source equality.
For the actual source 1/5 the central word is AAA; append the terminal B.
At y-degree one, the four-site multiaffine polynomial is

    a+d + 2ab+ac+bc+2ad+bd+2cd
        +3abc+3abd+3acd+3bcd+5abcd.

Homogenize it to degree four by z. Differentiate in a and z, and set d=0.

# Centered horizontal fibers and LC-positivity

Machine-authored research, request 65c4dfb883e140b0a62fddbffe247137.
The full pinned Conjecture63 remains open. No historical novelty is claimed.
Formal validation status is recorded separately in the final validation manifest.

Use the inherited, source-connected horizontal summands

    H(a,j,s,q) = choose(a-q,s) choose(s+q-1,q) choose(2s,j-q), s>0.

Out-of-range terms are zero. The inherited Lean horizontalTerm uses s-1.
For a fixed combined index k, pair the terms q and k-q in the coefficient of
F_s(t)^2-F_(s-1)(t)F_(s+1)(t). For q<k/2 the signed layer is

    D_q = 2 H_s(q)H_s(k-q)
          -H_(s-1)(q)H_(s+1)(k-q)-H_(s+1)(q)H_(s-1)(k-q).

For 2q=k use H_s(q)^2-H_(s-1)(q)H_(s+1)(q). Retain zeros.
The candidate condition is that every centered tail sum, from r to floor(k/2),
is nonnegative. This is equivalent, by grouping the two convolution orders,
to coefficientwise log-concavity after cutting off every q<r in each F_s.
The exact unsymmetrized convolution identity is formalized in
MarkovTruncatedFiber65c4; the regrouping equivalence in this paragraph is an
elementary paper derivation, not claimed as a separately checked Lean theorem.

This is the LC-positivity framework of Wang--Yeh. Their finite Abel argument
weights signed layers by a nonnegative increasing sequence. For a nonnegative
CrossLC sequence f, the centered products f(q)f(k-q) increase up to the center.
MarkovAbel65c4 checks this finite-sum transfer, including zero weights. Its tail
inequalities remain explicit hypotheses. They are NOT established for all H.
The source transfer from the new truncated-fiber proposition to every Pell
horizontal polygon triple is formalized using the inherited exact bridge.
It still has the truncated-fiber proposition as an unproved premise.

import Lean.CoreM

open Lean

unsafe def replayFromImports (module : Name) : IO Unit := do
  let mFile ← findOLean module
  unless (← mFile.pathExists) do
    throw <| IO.userError s!"object file '{mFile}' of module {module} does not exist"
  -- Load all module data parts (exported, server, private)
  let mut fnames := #[mFile]
  let sFile := OLeanLevel.server.adjustFileName mFile
  if (← sFile.pathExists) then
    fnames := fnames.push sFile
    let pFile := OLeanLevel.private.adjustFileName mFile
    if (← pFile.pathExists) then
      fnames := fnames.push pFile
  let parts ← readModuleDataParts fnames
  if h : parts.size = 0 then throw <| IO.userError "failed to read module data" else
  let (mod, _) := parts[0]
  let (_, s) ← importModulesCore mod.imports |>.run
  let env ← finalizeImport s mod.imports {} 0 false false (isModule := true)
  let mut newConstants := {}
  -- Collect constants from last ("most private") part, which subsumes all prior ones
  for name in parts[parts.size-1].1.constNames, ci in parts[parts.size-1].1.constants do
    newConstants := newConstants.insert name ci
  let env' ← env.replay newConstants
  env'.freeRegions

unsafe def replayFromFresh (module : Name) : IO Unit := do
  Lean.withImportModules #[{module}] {} fun env => do
    discard <| (← mkEmptyEnvironment).replay env.constants.map₁

/-- Read the name of the main module from the `lake-manifest`. -/
-- This has been copied from `ImportGraph.getCurrentModule` in the
-- https://github.com/leanprover-community/import-graph repository.
def getCurrentModule : IO Name := do
  match (← Lake.Manifest.load? ⟨"lake-manifest.json"⟩) with
  | none =>
    -- TODO: should this be caught?
    pure .anonymous
  | some manifest =>
    -- TODO: This assumes that the `package` and the default `lean_lib`
    -- have the same name up to capitalisation.
    -- Would be better to read the `.defaultTargets` from the
    -- `← getRootPackage` from `Lake`, but I can't make that work with the monads involved.
    return manifest.name.capitalize


/--
Run as e.g. `leanchecker` to check everything in the current project.
or e.g. `leanchecker Mathlib.Data.Nat` to check everything with module name
starting with `Mathlib.Data.Nat`.

This will replay all the new declarations from the target file into the `Environment`
as it was at the beginning of the file, using the kernel to check them.

You can also use `leanchecker --fresh Mathlib.Data.Nat.Prime.Basic`
to replay all the constants (both imported and defined in that file) into a fresh environment.
This can only be used on a single file.

This is not an external verifier, simply a tool to detect "environment hacking".
-/
unsafe def main (args : List String) : IO UInt32 := do
  -- Contributor's note: lean4lean is intended to have a CLI interface matching leanchecker,
  -- so if you want to make a change here please either make a sibling PR to
  -- https://github.com/digama0/lean4lean or ping @digama0 (Mario Carneiro) to go fix it.
  initSearchPath (← findSysroot)
  let (flags, args) := args.partition fun s => s.startsWith "-"
  let verbose := "-v" ∈ flags || "--verbose" ∈ flags
  let fresh := "--fresh" ∈ flags
  let targets ← do
    match args with
    | [] => pure [← getCurrentModule]
    | args => args.mapM fun arg => do
      let mod := arg.toName
      if mod.isAnonymous then
        throw <| IO.userError s!"Could not resolve module: {arg}"
      else
        pure mod
  let mut targetModules := []
  let sp ← searchPathRef.get
  for target in targets do
    let mut found := false
    for path in (← SearchPath.findAllWithExt sp "olean") do
      if let some m := (← searchModuleNameOfFileName path sp) then
        if !fresh && target.isPrefixOf m || target == m then
          targetModules := targetModules.insert m
          found := true
    if not found then
      throw <| IO.userError s!"Could not find any oleans for: {target}"
  if fresh then
    if targetModules.length != 1 then
      throw <| IO.userError s!"--fresh flag is only valid when specifying a single module:\n\
        {targetModules}"
    for m in targetModules do
      if verbose then IO.println s!"replaying {m} with --fresh"
      replayFromFresh m
  else
    let mut tasks := #[]
    for m in targetModules do
      tasks := tasks.push (m, ← IO.asTask (replayFromImports m))
    for (m, t) in tasks do
      if verbose then IO.println s!"replaying {m}"
      if let .error e := t.get then
        IO.eprintln s!"leanchecker found a problem in {m}"
        throw e
  return 0
